story_text.value:
A while back I recall being told it can't be done and won't be "Discord". To that, I have to admit, it's not Discord. It isn't designed in a way to profile it's users and it respects privacy.

There is still much work to do on this project, but it's in open beta with a web client so people can see how it works before committing to a desktop app download. Mobile apps will come later, if there is proven interest in this platform.

I don't care to monitize it. The only thing users will ever see is a non-intrusive "Please donate" badge at most, with the intentions to just keep the maintainer nodes and some official relays running.

There are no accounts. There is no way for me to see the messages. It is a platform that respects the user's privacy and asks nothing of it's user's.

Anyone can run the entire stack in their own hardware, in private, with no limitations on controlling their data.

It is open source (AGPLv3: https://github.com/hyperkubeorg/openarcanum/

And it's live right now for you to check out: https://openarcanum.org

I have a community server running that you may join with this community code (good for 30 days): ``` openarcanum-invite:ChACbbppkdJgXT5JFDYAyCMdEiBcigeLKcJMz5_6LKRhT_sSlYXITfl7Mctu2I5hRPmT1hogy8dDt7EjO6KG5Xz-ufvsCFWE8f_yQtaCFFYE8M83UcEiIXdzczovL3JlbGF5LTAxLm9wZW5hcmNhbnVtLm9yZy93cyIhd3NzOi8vcmVsYXktMDIub3BlbmFyY2FudW0ub3JnL3dzKhhBMnJXa1BYRGRkbHVsVC13V1ZTbDg2OHcyEEhhY2tlciBOZXdzIENyZXc ```

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I'm Darin. You might know me from my work at Webflow (YC S13) and currently Ploy (YC P26).

Sunlight is the way I imagined the Mac working before I got my 1st-gen MacBook Air in high school (2008). I had looked at a bunch of Apple videos of Mission Control (Exposé back then) and somehow decided it worked like an infinite canvas. I even told my mom about it! I guess it stuck with me.

Windowing on the Mac is so good it's one of those "if it ain't broke don't fix it" things. And yet, it always felt lacking. So Sunlight reimagines it from first principles:

- 355"+ virtual desktop

- 120fps, fully native

- Multi-touch interactions

- Guides, grids and haptics

- Minimap

- ⌘Tab and Mission Control work as usual

- Works with your Dock, widgets and desktop

- Collision detection and magnetic windows

- Tiling and saved layouts

- Deeply customizable

- ...and much more (including agent support) coming soon

Free and open source, forever.

Launch demo (2:34): https://youtu.be/NSerIT8zRpw

Repo: https://github.com/spacefarm-digital/sunlight

title.value: Show HN: Sunlight – the camera-based infinite canvas window manager for Mac

story_text.value:
At work, we're leaning heavily into agentic development. I've always used tmux to manage my work and now I'm using it to organize my 30+ Claude sessions.

I wanted a simple read-only dashboard that would identify which of my sessions needed attention and also fit my vim-based navigation workflows. There are times when all I remember is a name or phrase from a conversation. The search feature was built to address this by searching the contents of every transcript, not just session titles.

Just curious if other devs are experiencing similar issues and whether this approach is helpful at all. Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: ccfleet, a quiet, tmux-native Claude Code dashboard

story_text.value:
I've built this completely solo over the last month. I posted here once a few weeks ago at a very early stage, but since it has greatly matured and I feel is legitimate for a repost.

We all know "We stand on the shoulders of giants", but who's shoulders exactly? This application is meant to help anyone answer this for themselves, their advisor, or just a scholar they are curious about - anywhere in the world.

Current Challenges I'm facing are largely surrounding PDF extractions which I aim to complete as many templates as possible to reduce the token costs incurred running the worst of them through an LLM for ingestion.

I also happen to be LFW, if you or someone you know needs an engineer who doesn't need hand holding to drive from concept, to data, through pixels and delivers scalable, distributable production solutions- Reach out, I'd love to connect! (My Resume is available on the website through the Toast).

The Goal with this app is that it becomes a legitimate reference and core hub/registry of information alongside sources like Google Scholar, Wikidata, OpenAlex, etc.

Would Love Feedback, Advice, Feature requests, even "Hey I tried to look my self/friend/advisor up and couldnt find them, or noticed a mistake" - ABSOLUTELY ALL FEEDBACK WILL BE RESPONDED TO AND ACTED UPON IMMEDIATELY - Thankyou for Checking it out!

story_text.value:
Hi HN! My company Regbase tracks regulatory developments around the world for compliance teams at major corporations. Ahead of the midterm elections we decided to do an in-depth survey of all state and local regulations around data centers.

We built an interactive map showing the data center policies across the United States. It covers all 50 states and 1,462 localities across legislation, regulations and executive orders. We collected and analyzed the data using our platform. Every result has a link to the official source so you can read the policy for yourself.

Here's some interesting things we learned:

- Moratoriums (temporary bans) are the most common instrument. We counted 1,010 in total with an average duration of 10 months.

- Starting around October 2025, most policies switched from tax incentives to bans and restrictions. This correlates with increased energy prices and worsening public sentiment towards AI.

- When construction is allowed, it's very common for protections to be put in place particularly around electricity and less for water. Many of the bans are actually refusals to issue these licenses.

We would love your feedback! In particular please let us know if there is any other data that would be useful or interesting to see.

title.value: Show HN: We mapped data center regulations across 50 states and 1,462 localities

story_text.value:
Hi guys,

I built a tool www.lovespreadsheets.com earlier this year and a huge problem we kept running into is processing messy, real-world, complex spreadsheets for AI agents.

Even a "medium" sized spreadsheet converts to about 1m+ tokens if read fully, which immediately blows up the current context windows of most models. So I noticed most agents sample data from spreadsheets in chunks instead.

So I (& Claude) built this library Sheetgraph, https://github.com/asharma327/sheetgraph, to compress spreadsheets (~100x compression) while still maintaining their structure (like a dependency graph for formulas) & other relevant metadata such as macros, cell data types, formatting. There is a zipped full workbook of the spreadsheet as well for the agent to lookup data as needed.

Still rough around the edges so would love any feedback on both the idea and any details. This is used in our primary product + services platform Love Spreadsheets so we are actively maintaining and improving it.

Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: Sheetgraph, AI agents can understand complex spreadsheets
